source.title: Adaptive Batch Size Schedules for Distributed Training of Language Models with Data and Model Parallelism
source.authors: Tim Tsz-Kit Lau; Weijian Li; Chen-Wei Xu; Han Liu; Mladen Kolar

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation affecting the reported experiments.
record.tranche_reason: Tests batch-size conditions bearing on V5 using adaptive norm-test schedules and validation loss in language-model pretraining; this is a different batch-size intervention from the version's cited studies.
record.gate_note: The paper's discussion of cited studies on batch sizes, optimizers and generalization is prior work, not this paper's result. Rows below cover the reported validation losses in Tables 1–3; training loss, steps, average batch size and wall-clock time are omitted because they do not directly measure V5's held-out performance.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares held-out loss across batch sizes and schedules in Llama-family pretraining. Each run processes 2,000,000 sequences with otherwise shared hyperparameters, testing V5 under equal data exposure in a new setting.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase broadly captures the authors' claims, but needs qualification: selected adaptive schedules improve validation loss and training efficiency, whereas several TinyLlama settings perform worse than fixed batches. The authors present these as short proof-of-concept runs, establish a convergence result under theoretical assumptions, and report no downstream evaluation because the models were insufficiently pretrained.
record.recipe_differences: Uses adaptive norm-test batch-size schedules with AdamW for Llama-family language-model pretraining, rather than the original studies' fixed-batch comparisons or other cited batch-size interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Validation loss varies with adaptive-schedule η, model, and batch-size schedule. OpenLlama 3B used sequence length 512; MicroLlama and TinyLlama used 2048. The paper notes η also varies with base learning rate and training-data quality, but does not report an experiment varying those factors.
record.problems: The authors describe the experiments as proofs of concept and state that the models were not pretrained for sufficient tokens. Evaluation is validation loss only, estimated by 100 iterations for MicroLlama; no downstream benchmarks are reported. No uncertainty estimates are provided.
record.rows_left_out: None of the numerical validation-loss rows in Tables 1–3 were left out. Figure-only curves are not separately extracted because the corresponding tabulated validation-loss results are recorded.

untested.parts: Convolutional versus fully connected image architectures.
Held-out performance comparisons between optimizers and tuning budgets; all experimental runs use AdamW.

Image classifiers, fully pretrained models, downstream performance, longer-training recovery, batch-dependent learning-rate scaling, and normalization or regularization interventions. A workload-dependent batch-size threshold is not established.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its correlation with generalization gaps.

missing.what: The separate 61M-parameter vanilla-transformer experiment compares batches 512, 1024, 2048, and 4096 and is explicitly presented as showing a batch-size generalization penalty. It has no corresponding table or extracted row; numerical curve ordering cannot be recovered reliably from the supplied text.

record.verdict_notes: All tabulated validation-loss values match the supplied text. Appendices C.1–C.3 specify equal budgets of 2,000,000 sequences, sample-based learning-rate warmup, and no optimizer scaling rule. This tests held-out loss under fixed data exposure, without isolating a generalization mechanism from optimization progress: larger batches also have substantially worse training losses. For fixed-batch rows, states describe the comparative penalty; for schedule rows, states describe recovery of that penalty. Absent recovery does not mean the batch-size penalty is absent. Partial recovery supports V5's explicit shrinkage clause rather than automatically limiting it. No uncertainty estimates or repeated-run variation are reported.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps past interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image models.

Image classifiers; language models beyond the reported Llama-family models; whether the same epoch budget suffices under different schedules; the roles of learning-rate scaling, warmup, normalization or regularization changes.
Sharpness or other measured properties tracking the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.
